title: Truthfulness of Scripture
definition: The Truthfulness of Scripture means God’s Word is true in all that it teaches because God Himself is true and cannot lie.
summary: The Truthfulness of Scripture means God’s Word is true in all that it teaches because God Himself is true and cannot lie.
christFocus: Jesus is the Truth, and He confirmed the truthfulness of God’s Word while fulfilling the promises, prophecies, and saving message Scripture declares.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Scripture is truthful because it comes from the God who is truthful. God does not deceive, distort, or speak carelessly. His Word reveals reality as He sees it, not merely as people feel it or as culture defines it.

The truthfulness of Scripture gives believers a firm place to stand. God’s Word tells the truth about Him, about humanity, about sin, about salvation, about judgment, and about hope. It tells us the truth we may not want to hear and the truth we desperately need to receive.

Jesus prayed, “Your word is truth.” He did not treat Scripture as uncertain or disposable. He trusted it, taught it, fulfilled it, and sent His people to proclaim the truth revealed in it. The truthful Word leads us to the faithful Savior.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People who have been lied to, manipulated, or disappointed often struggle to know what can be trusted. The truthfulness of Scripture gives the wounded and confused believer a foundation that does not shift with emotion, pressure, or human failure.

This doctrine also corrects the idea that truth is whatever a person sincerely feels. Sincerity cannot save, heal, or guide unless it is brought under the truth God has spoken.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Let Scripture tell the truth about God, about you, and about the world. When God’s Word confronts a lie you have believed, do not cling to the lie for comfort; ask the Holy Spirit to renew your mind and lead you into the freedom of Christ.
